---
title: "3. Meet the inputs: Human stool study"
---

## Locate the three files

| File in `data/zackular/` | What to inspect |
|---|---|
| `feature-counts.tsv` | Feature IDs in rows; sample IDs in columns; integer read counts |
| `sample-metadata.tsv` | One row per sample, with sample ID, group and available covariates |
| `taxonomy.tsv` | Each feature ID and its supplied lineage or display label |

Pick one sample and find it in counts and metadata. Pick one feature and find
it in counts and taxonomy. Row order is not evidence of a match; IDs are.

Read [the study and provenance notes](../../99-appendix.qmd). The input was
exported from a packaged count object; the original human study had 90 samples
in three groups. Our comparison retains all available healthy and carcinoma
samples. Two absent adenoma records do not affect this selection.

Metadata preserve age, sex, collection location and original labels. Sex
whitespace was removed and f/m expanded; a location typo was harmonised before
modelling. The participant-ID field in the original spreadsheet is empty;
do not claim a separately verified participant crosswalk.

Taxonomy identifies OTU annotations, sometimes only at family level. Several
OTUs can share a genus name. Do not collapse them by copying legend labels.

**Your task:** record assay, sample unit, group definition and one missing piece of information that matters for interpretation.
